limitations: One unprofiled operation run per browser and venue; three separately profiled Chrome 003 repetitions.
Headless hardware WebGL, 1440x900 viewport, DPR2; actual buffer 2160x1350 after the existing DPR cap. Not physical input-to-display latency.
GPU queries measured in separate runs; do not add their duration to CPU submission or mix them into the unprofiled baseline.
Long render gaps in on-demand idle or transition phases are not automatically dropped animation frames.
CPU profiles show aggregate self-time, not the cause of an individual unprofiled spike. Legacy-generated engine URLs can be blank.
Loading/switching uses development output; operation/GPU uses source. Fresh browser context does not clear OS caches or guarantee cold disk.
Room clients and server share a process on loopback; timer delay is a blocking proxy, not an internet or concurrency test.
No fixed power/thermal state or OS-wide idle guarantee; no production behavior or rendering changes made.
Venue scene-ready timing observes the URL commit after switch completion; click-to-interactive includes automation polling.
